text: Agreed to pace rolling endurance rides steadily on climbs rather than surging, using conversational breathing and comfortable cadence as effort checks.
The final riser felt harder than usual after a long day on the athlete's feet and into a headwind; this was attributed to conditions and accumulated fatigue, not declining fitness.
For windy exposed river sections, agreed to tuck lower on the bars and eat earlier to preserve energy in the final hour, while monitoring hand and shoulder comfort as volume rises.
Mild leg heaviness on day two of back-to-back rides cleared after 20 minutes of easy spinning, so no plan adjustment was needed.
The back-to-back ride plan remains unchanged; if second-day heaviness ever lasts beyond 30 minutes, shorten that ride rather than push through and accumulate excess fatigue.
For rides over two hours, agreed on one bottle per hour, food every 30 minutes, and a larger breakfast before sustained climbing; practice this first on easy rides so it is familiar on long weekends.
A recovery route with fewer junctions allowed genuinely easy riding and relaxed breathing throughout.
Recovery spins will start from the park side of town because the route has fewer junctions, and easy days will remain protected even when the schedule is busy.
